open_points.subject: Upgrade of existing access tables from full-pair uniqueness
open_points.text: Creates the tables when absent; never drops, alters, commits, rolls back or closes.
open_points.question: How will an existing deployment whose access tables still have the former full-pair UNIQUE constraints be converted to active-only uniqueness without losing revoked history?
options: Rebuild the three affected tables in a deployment migration, preserve every row, and install partial unique indexes for active records
Create replacement tables with the new constraints, copy and verify every row, then atomically switch them into service
consequences: An in-place migration can preserve identifiers and history with a shorter operational path, but requires a transactional SQLite table rebuild and deployment downtime or locking.
Replacement tables permit explicit verification before cutover, but require more storage, a coordinated switch, and cleanup of the former tables.
open_points.requirement: INV-009: at most one active record per (staff_id, project_id) assignment, per (viewer_id, project_id) grant and per (service_principal_id, project_id) grant; revoked records of the pair stay, and a new grant after revocation is a new record
open_points.default_guess: Use one transactional deployment migration that rebuilds all three affected tables, preserves every record and identifier, and installs active-only partial unique indexes.

witness.initial: A deployed database was created under the former schema and contains a revoked access record for a pair.
events: The new release is deployed without recreating the database.
An administrator attempts to give the pair access again.
outcomes: A deployment migration removes the obsolete full-pair constraint, so the new active record is created and the revoked history remains.
No migration runs, so the obsolete constraint rejects the insert and the administrator receives a persistence failure.

set_aside.subject: StaffProjectAssignment uniqueness
set_aside.question: Must `create_staff_access_schema` instead guarantee uniqueness only for active assignments, so `assign_staff_project` can create a new record after revocation while still refusing a second active record?
options: Replace full-pair uniqueness with uniqueness limited to active assignments
Keep full-pair uniqueness, which makes the promised post-revocation assignment impossible
set_aside.default_guess: Replace the full-pair constraint with a partial unique constraint for active assignments.

witness.initial: A staff/project pair has one revoked StaffProjectAssignment and no active assignment.
events: An administrator calls assign_staff_project for that pair after Registry validation succeeds.
outcomes: The changed operation obligation creates and returns a new active assignment while preserving the revoked record.
The schema obligation rejects the insert because the staff/project pair is already present, producing PersistenceError and no new assignment.

set_aside.subject: ProducerProjectGrant uniqueness
set_aside.text: (`service_principal_id`, `project_id`) of a grant and (`service_principal_id`, `key_version`) of a credential are unique.
set_aside.question: Must `create_producer_identity_schema` retain credential key-version uniqueness but limit producer-grant pair uniqueness to active grants, so `grant_producer_project` can create a new record after revocation?
options: Keep credential key-version uniqueness and replace full grant-pair uniqueness with uniqueness limited to active grants
Keep full grant-pair uniqueness, which makes the promised post-revocation grant impossible
set_aside.default_guess: Keep credential key-version uniqueness and use a partial unique constraint for active producer grants.
